50314.subject: Further Mathematics
50314.explanation:
The domain of a function refers to the regions where the function is defined or has a value on a particular region.

\(\frac{4x^{2} - 1}{\sqrt{9x^{2} + 1}}\) has a domain defined on all set of real numbers because the function is defined on the set of real numbers when the denominator \(\sqrt{9x^{2} + 1} \geq 0\).

\(\sqrt{9x^{2} + 1} \geq 0 \implies 9x^{2} + 1 \geq 0\) which because of the square sign has a value for all values of x, be it negative or positive.

50316.question_text: Given that \(f(x) = 3x^{2} -  12x + 12\) and \(f(x) = 3\), find the values of x.

50317.subject: Further Mathematics
50317.question_text: A binary operation * is defined on the set of real numbers, by \(a * b = \frac{a}{b} + \frac{b}{a}\). If \((\sqrt{x} + 1) * (\sqrt{x} - 1) = 4\), find the value of x.

50318.subject: Further Mathematics
50318.question_text: If \(4x^{2} + 5kx + 10\) is a perfect square, find the value of k.
50318.explanation:
\(4x^{2} + 5kx + 10 = (2x + \sqrt{10})^{2}\)

Expanding the right hand side equation, we have

\(4x^{2} + 4x\sqrt{10} + 10\)

Comparing with the left hand side, we have

\(5k = 4\sqrt{10}  \implies k = \frac{4}{5}\sqrt{10}\)

50320.subject: Further Mathematics
50320.question_text: If the polynomial \(f(x) = 3x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 7x + 5\) is divided by (x - 1), find the remainder.

50329.subject: Further Mathematics
50329.question_text: \(P = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}, Q = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12}, R = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}\) are subsets of \(U = {1, 2, 3, ... , 12}\). Which of the following statements is true?
50329.explanation:
All the statements are false except option C.

\(R \cap P = {3, 5, 7} and R \cap U = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}\) 

\(\therefore (R \cap P) \subset (R \cap U)\)

50331.subject: Further Mathematics
50331.question_text: If \(\log_{3}a - 2 = 3\log_{3}b\), express a in terms of b.
50331.explanation:
\(\log_{3}a - 2 = 3\log_{3}b\)

Using the laws of logarithm, we know that \( 2 = 2\log_{3}3 = \log_{3}3^{2}\)

\(\therefore \log_{3}a - \log_{3}3^{2} = \log_{3}b^{3}\)

= \(\log_{3}(\frac{a}{3^{2}}) = \log_{3}b^{3}   \implies  \frac{a}{9} = b^{3}\)

\(\implies a = 9b^{3}\)

50339.subject: Further Mathematics
50339.question_text: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of \(2x^{2} - 5x + 6 = 0\), find the equation whose roots are \((\alpha + 1)\) and \((\beta + 1)\).
50339.explanation:
Note: Given the sum of the roots and its product, we can get the equation using the formula:

\(x^{2} - (\alpha + \beta)x + (\alpha\beta) = 0\). This will be used later on in the course of our solution.

Given equation: \(2x^{2} - 5x + 6 = 0; a = 2, b = -5, c = 6\).

\(\alpha + \beta = \frac{-b}{a} = \frac{-(-5)}{2} = \frac{5}{2}\)

\(\alpha\beta = \frac{c}{a} = \frac{6}{2} = 3\)

Given the roots of the new equation as \((\alpha + 1)\) and \((\beta + 1)\), their sum and product will be

\((\alpha + 1) + (\beta + 1) = \alpha + \beta + 2 = \frac{5}{2} + 2 = \frac{9}{2} = \frac{-b}{a}\)

\((\alpha + 1)(\beta + 1) = \alpha\beta + \alpha + \beta + 1 = 3 + \frac{5}{2} + 1 = \frac{13}{2} = \frac{c}{a}\)

The new equation is given by: \(x^{2} - (\frac{-b}{a})x + (\frac{c}{a}) = 0\)

= \(x^{2} - (\frac{9}{2})x + \frac{13}{2} = 2x^{2} - 9x + 13 = 0\)

50346.subject: Further Mathematics
50346.question_text: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of the equation \(2x^{2} + 5x + n = 0\), such that \(\alpha\beta = 2\), find the value of n.
50346.explanation:
An equation can be written as \(x^{2} - (\alpha + \beta)x + (\alpha\beta) = 0\)

Making the coefficient of \(x^{2}\) = 1 in the given equation, we have

\(x^{2} + \frac{5}{2}x + \frac{n}{2} = 0\)

Comparing, we have \(\alpha\beta = \frac{n}{2} = 2 \implies n = 4\)

50361.subject: Further Mathematics
50361.question_text: Find the coefficient of \(x^{3}\) in the binomial expansion of \((x - \frac{3}{x^{2}})^{9}\).

50362.subject: Further Mathematics
50362.question_text: The general term of an infinite sequence 9, 4, -1, -6,... is \(u_{r} = ar + b\). Find the values of a and b.
50362.explanation:
The terms of the sequence can be written as : \(u_{r} = ar + b\) in this case, being that they have a regular common difference for each of the r terms.

We can rewrite the sequence as \(a + b, 2a + b, 3a + b,...\) where a is the common difference of the sequence and b is a given constant gotten by solving

\(a + b = 9\) or \(2a + b = 4\) or any other one. 

The common difference here is 4 - 9 = -1 - 4 = -5.

\(-5 + b = 9 \implies b = 9 + 5 = 14\)

\(\therefore\) The equation can be written as \(u_{r} = -5r + 14\).

50363.subject: Further Mathematics
50363.question_text: If \(\begin{vmatrix}  k & k \\ 4 & k \end{vmatrix} + \begin{vmatrix}  2 & 3 \\ -1 & k \end{vmatrix} = 6\), find the value of the constant k, where k > 0.
50363.explanation:
\(\begin{vmatrix} k & k \\ 4 & k \end{vmatrix} + \begin{vmatrix}  2 & 3 \\ -1 & k \end{vmatrix} = 6\)

\(\begin{vmatrix} k & k \\ 4 & k \end{vmatrix} = (k^{2} - 4k)\)

\(\begin{vmatrix}  2 & 3 \\ -1 & k \end{vmatrix} = (2k + 3)\)

\(\therefore (k^{2} - 4k) + (2k + 3) = k^{2} - 2k + 3 = 6\)

\(k^{2} - 2k - 3 = 0\), factorising, we have \(k + 1 = 0\) or \(k - 3 = 0\)

Since k > 0, k = 3.

50364.subject: Further Mathematics
50364.question_text: How many numbers greater than 150 can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
50364.explanation:
Note that every 4- digit and 5- digit numbers formed is greater than 150. Therefore, \(^{5}P_{5} + ^{5}P_{4} = \frac{5!}{(5 - 5)!} + \frac{5!}{(5 - 4)!} = 120 + 120 = 240\) numbers are greater than 150 already.

Among the 3- digit numbers, the numbers 123, 124, 125, 132, 134, 135, 142, 143 and 145 are removed from the ones that meet the criterion so we have:

\(^{5}P_{3} - 9 = \frac{5!}{(5 - 3)!} = 60 - 9 = 51 \implies 240 + 51 = 291\) numbers are greater than 150.

50365.subject: Further Mathematics
50365.question_text: The first term of a Geometric Progression (GP) is \(\frac{3}{4}\), If the product of the second and third terms of the sequence is 972, find its common ratio.
50365.explanation:
Recall, the terms of a GP is given by \(T_{n} = ar^{n - 1}\)

Given, \(T_{1} = a = \frac{3}{4}\) and \(T_{2} \times T_{3} = ar \times ar^{2} = 972\)

\(\implies \frac{3}{4}r \times \frac{3}{4}r^{2} = \frac{9}{16}r^{3} = 972\)

\(r^{3} = \frac{972 \times 16}{9} = 1728  \implies r = \sqrt[3]{1728} = 12\)

50366.subject: Further Mathematics
50366.explanation:
Given \(\sin \theta = \frac{3}{5}  \implies opp = 3, hyp = 5\)

Using Pythagoras' Theorem, we have \( adj = \sqrt{5^{2} - 3^{2}} = \sqrt{16}  = 4\)

\(\therefore \cos \theta = \frac{4}{5}, 0° < \theta < 90°\)

In the quadrant where \(180° - \theta\) lies is the 2nd quadrant and here, only \(\sin \theta = +ve\).

\(\therefore \cos (180 - \theta) = -ve = \frac{-4}{5}\)

50367.subject: Further Mathematics
50367.question_text: Find the radius of the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 8x - 2y + 1 = 0\).
50367.explanation:
Given the equation of the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 8x - 2y + 1 = 0\).

The equation of a circle is given as \((x - a)^{2} + (y - b)^{2} = r^{2}\)

Expanding, we have \(x^{2} - 2ax + a^{2} + y^{2} - 2by + b^{2} = r^{2} \equiv x^{2} - 2ax + y^{2} - 2by = r^{2} - a^{2} - b^{2}\)

Comparing the RHS of the equation above with the equation rewritten as \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 8x - 2y = -1\), we have

\(-2a = -8; -2b = -2 \implies a = 4, b = 1\)

\(\therefore r^{2} - 4^{2} - 1^{2} = -1 \implies r^{2} = -1 + 16 + 1 = 16\)

\(r = \sqrt{16} = 4\)

50368.subject: Further Mathematics
50368.question_text: In how many ways can the letters of the word 'ELECTIVE' be arranged?
50368.explanation:
The word has 8 letters with one letter repeated 3 times, therefore we have:

\(\frac{8!}{3!} = 6720\) ways.

50369.question_text: If the determinant of the matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} 2 & x \\ 3 & 5 \end{pmatrix} = 13\), find the value of x.

50371.subject: Further Mathematics
50371.question_text: Find the equation to the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x - 2y = 0\) at the point (1, 3).
50371.explanation:
We are given the equation \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x - 2y = 0\)

\(y = x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x - 2y \)

Using the method of implicit differentiation, 

\(\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = 2x + 2y\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} - 4 - 2\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x}\)

For the tangent, \(\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = 0\),

\(\therefore 2x + 2y\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} - 4 - 2\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = 0\)

\((2y - 2)\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = 4 - 2x \implies \frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = \frac{4 - 2x}{2y - 2}\)

At (1, 3), \(\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = \frac{4 - 2(1)}{2(3) - 2} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\)

Equation: \(\frac{y - 3}{x - 1} = \frac{1}{2} \implies 2y - 6 = x - 1\)

= \(2y - x - 6 + 1 = 2y - x - 5 = 0\)

50372.subject: Further Mathematics
50372.question_text: Given that \(y = x(x + 1)^{2}\), calculate the maximum value of y.
50372.explanation:
To find the maximum value, we can use the second derivative test where, given \(f(x)\), the second derivative < 0, makes it a maximum value.

\(x(x + 1)^{2} = x(x^{2} + 2x + 1) = x^{3} + 2x^{2} + x\)

\(\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = 3x^{2} + 4x + 1 = 0\)

Solving, we have \( x = \frac{-1}{3}\) or \(-1\).

\(\frac{\mathrm d^{2} y}{\mathrm d x^{2}} = 6x + 4\)

When \(x = \frac{-1}{3}, \frac{\mathrm d^{2} y}{\mathrm d x^{2}} = 2 > 0\)

When \(x = -1, \frac{\mathrm d^{2} y}{\mathrm d x^{2}} = -2 < 0\)

At maximum value of x being -1, \(y = -1(-1 + 1)^{2} = 0\)

50373.subject: Further Mathematics
50373.question_text: The midpoint of M(4, -1) and N(x, y) is P(3, -4). Find the coordinates of N.

50374.subject: Further Mathematics
50374.question_text: Find the stationary point of the curve \(y = 3x^{2} - 2x^{3}\).
50374.explanation:
\(y = 3x^{2} - 2x^{3}\)

\(\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = 6x - 6x^{2} = 0 \implies 6x(1 - x) = 0\)

\(x = 0, 1\), when x = 1, y = 0.

when x = 1, y = 0.

The stationary point is (1, 0)

50378.subject: Further Mathematics
50378.question_text: Out of 70 schools, 42 of them can be attended by boys and 35 can be attended by girls. If a pupil is selected at random from these schools, find the probability that he/ she is from a mixed school.
50378.explanation:
Let the number of mixed schools be S

The number of boys only = 42 - S

The number of girls only = 35 - S

(42 - S) + S + (35 - S) = 77 - S = 70

\(\implies\) S = 7

\(Probability = \frac{7}{70} = \frac{1}{10}\)

50380.question_text: Given that \(a = i - 3j\) and \(b = -2i + 5j\) and \(c = 3i - j\), calculate \(|a - b + c|\).

50381.subject: Further Mathematics
50381.question_text: What is the probability of obtaining a head and a six when a fair coin and and a die are tossed together?
50381.explanation:
\(\text{p(a head and a six)} = \text{p(a head)} \times \text{p(a six)}\)

= \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}\).

50383.subject: Further Mathematics
50383.question_text: A body of mass 28g, initially at rest is acted upon by a force, F Newtons. If it attains a velocity of \(5.4ms^{-1}\) in 18 seconds, find the value of F.
50383.explanation:
\(F = mass \times acceleration\) but \(accl = \frac{v - u}{t}\)

\(\therefore F = m(\frac{v - u}{t})\)

\(Mass = 28g = 0.028kg\)

\(v = 5.4 ms^{-1}; u = 0; t = 18secs\)

\(\therefore F = 0.028(\frac{5.4 - 0}{18}) = 0.028 \times 0.3 = 0.0084N\)

50384.subject: Further Mathematics
50384.question_text: Find the angle between forces of magnitude 7N and 4N if their resultant has a magnitude of 9N.

50385.subject: Further Mathematics
50385.question_text: Find the constant term in the binomial expansion \((2x^{2} + \frac{1}{x})^{9}\)
50385.explanation:
Let the power of \(2x^{2}\) be t and the power of \(\frac{1}{x} \equiv x^{-1}\) = 9 - t.

\((2x^{2})^{t}(x^{-1})^{9 - t} = x^{0}\)

Dealing with x alone, we have

\((x^{2t})(x^{-9 + t}) = x^{0} \implies 2t - 9 + t = 0\)

\(3t - 9 = 0 \therefore t = 3\)

The binomial expansion is then,

\(^{9}C_{3} (2x^{2})^{3}(x^{-1})^{6} = \frac{9!}{(9-3)! 3!} \times 2^{3}\)

= 84 x 8

= 672

50386.subject: Further Mathematics
50386.question_text: A particle starts from rest and moves through a distance \(S = 12t^{2} - 2t^{3}\) metres in time t seconds. Find its acceleration in 1 second.
50386.explanation:
\(\frac{\mathrm d s(t)}{\mathrm d t} = v(t)\) and \(\frac{\mathrm d v(t)}{\mathrm d t} = a(t)\)

\(\therefore v(t) = \frac{\mathrm d (12t^{2} - 2t^{3})}{\mathrm d t} = 24t - 6t^{2}\)

\(\frac{\mathrm d (24t - 6t^{2})}{\mathrm d t} = 24 - 12t = a(t)\)

\(a(1) = 24 - 12(1) = 24 - 12 = 12ms^{-2}\)

50387.subject: Further Mathematics
50387.question_text: A car is moving at 120\(kmh^{-1}\). Find its speed in \(ms^{-1}\).
